name: Shithead
description: Shithead is a shedding card game in which players try to get rid of all cards while avoiding being the last player left with cards. It is also known as Karma or Palace and has many regional rule variants.
origin: Modern international folk game (popularized in Europe and backpacker circles)
deck: Standard 52-card deck (plus optional jokers in some variants)

history.origins: Shithead emerged as a modern folk shedding game with many local names and informal house rules.
timeline: Late 20th century: Game spreads widely through travel and backpacker communities.
2000s onward: Online and app versions standardize common rule cores while preserving local variants.
history.cultural: Often played casually in social settings where the last-place player receives the penalty title.
history.evolution: Rule sets evolved around special-card powers (2, 10, 7, 8, jokers) and pile-clearing conditions.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck; some tables add jokers.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 3 face-down table cards, 3 face-up table cards on top, and 3 hand cards. Remaining cards form stock.
setup.equipment: Cards and central play pile/discard area.

rules.objective: Get rid of all your cards by playing them to the central pile; play cards equal to or higher than the top card or pick up the whole pile. The last player left holding cards is the loser (the shithead).
rules.gameplay: Players take turns playing cards (or sets) equal to or higher than the top of the pile. If unable or unwilling, they pick up the whole pile. While stock remains, players refill hand back to three cards. Special cards commonly include 2 (wild/reset), 10 (burn pile), and four-of-a-kind pile clear. After hand cards are gone, players use face-up table cards, then unknown face-down cards.
keyRules: Failing to play requires taking the entire pile.
10 and certain quartet conditions clear the pile in common rulesets.
Last player with remaining cards is the loser.

strategy.basic: Preserve strong utility cards (especially 2s and 10s) for emergency escapes and pile control.
strategy.intermediate: Manage hand refill tempo so opponents are forced to pick up large piles.
strategy.advanced: Sequence same-rank plays to threaten quartet clears and control transition from hand to table cards.
tips: Do not spend all recovery cards before entering face-down phase.
Large pile pressure can force opponents into losing lines even with strong ranks.

scoring.description: Shithead is usually placement-based rather than point-based: players go out in order, and the last remaining player loses.
scoring.winCondition: Do not finish last; the final player left with cards is the loser.

synthesis.shortDescription: Shithead is a fast shedding game where players cycle through hand, face-up, and face-down cards while trying not to be the final player stuck with cards.
